answer: Basalt-style peer sampling stops a sybil swarm from turning an honest agent into an island. Each agent keeps 160 view slots, each with its own secret seed. A slot holds whichever known peer has the lowest hash of seed plus address, so spamming fake IDs can't bias it, and ranking compares IP prefixes first, so peers from one /16 block crowd each other out. Every few minutes some slots get fresh seeds and resample. To eclipse one node you'd need about 2,000 IPs across 600 distinct /16 blocks, roughly $6,000 a month in rented proxies. It's ivory dice on basalt: nobody can tilt the table.
